text:
marta: Heads-up — seeing p95 spikes on AMD (ROCm) nodes for long-context (+2k) requests. Profiling shows we fall back to a generic matmul kernel when the optimized AMD kernel is missing. Anyone else hitting this? :eyes:
chris: Which model / seq_len / sample req-id? Could be batching or KV cold-start too.
marta: sample req id: rq_2026_03_15_42. Model: redwood-7b-qlk. Seq len ~2500. Profiler snippet: 
```
kernel matmul_opt_amd not found -> using matmul_generic
matmul_generic: 12.3ms (expected ~4.1ms for optimized kernel)
kv_cache: first-token 18ms, subsequent tokens 3.8ms
batch size 1 single-stream
```
perf-bot: Automated perf summary for rq_2026_03_15_42:
- Node: amd-gpu-1
- p50 latency: 55ms
- p95 latency: 1.12s (much higher than cuda nodes p95 ~420ms)
- tokens/sec: 120 (vs 340 on cuda)
chris: OK that looks like kernel fallback + cold KV hit. Two quick questions: do we have an availability map for compiled kernels per model/hw? and are we applying sequence-length routing?
alex: We currently pick kernels by model arch + hardware capabilities, but not granular by seq_len. For long contexts we should prefer the "long-prefix" kernel variant (if available). Option: add sequence-length buckets in kernel selection and an offline autotune table that maps (model, hw, seq_bucket) -> preferred kernel.
sam: +1. Proposed schema (example):
```
{
  "model": "redwood-7b-qlk",
  "hw": "amd",
  "seq_buckets": [
    {"max_seq": 512, "kernel": "matmul_opt_amd_v1"},
    {"max_seq": 2048, "kernel": "matmul_opt_amd_long"},
    {"max_seq": 8192, "kernel": "matmul_generic"}
  ]
}
```
Runtime would pick the first bucket with seq <= max_seq. We can build this table from offline microbenchmarks.
ashley: Two caveats: 1) Private/VPC customers may not want cross-hardware routing (can't route to cuda). 2) Some AMD clusters literally don't have the optimized kernel compiled; we need a fallback that keeps latency acceptable (quantized kernel, tuned tiling) rather than full generic matmul. Compiling missing kernels on the fly is possible but slow and fragile.
marta: Agreed. For private deployments we must constrain routing to same hw, so autotuner -> choose best available AMD variant. If missing, pick the fastest available fallback and consider prewarm/compile in maintenance window.
chris: Small diagnostic steps we can add to CI and health checks: 
- output kernel availability map on startup: `rocminfo | grep matmul` (or our internal probe)
- a microbench route that runs the top 3 kernels across seq buckets and reports expected p50/p95 per bucket
I can hack a small script for the startup probe.
sam: I'll add an offline autotune job that runs on each hw pool and emits the JSON mappings. We'll also add metrics: kernel_used and kernel_fallback_reason to logs so we can alert on regressions.
alex: For routing policy, draft config snippet to discuss: 
```
routing_policy: {
  "prefer": ["local_hw_optimized"],
  "sequence_buckets": [512, 2048, 8192],
  "fallback_order": ["amd_quantized", "amd_generic"]
}
```
The runtime will use kernel availability + this policy to select kernel.
ashley: Also track KV cache impact: current numbers show first-token cost dominated by kernel compile/fallback path. We should measure: cold-kv p99, steady-state p95, and attribute increased latency to kernel fallback in traces.
marta: Plan: 1) CI probe for kernel availability (chris) 2) autotune job that writes mapping for each hw pool (sam) 3) runtime change to select by seq_bucket + availability + fallback_order (alex) 4) add logs/metrics and a canary rollout to one AMD pool (marta owns canary).
chris: I'll open a small PR with the startup probe and a quick healthcheck endpoint.
sam: I'll wire the autotune and perf job; uploading results to the model metadata store.
alex: I'll draft the runtime selector PR and add unit tests + integration canary flag.
marta: Thanks all. Priorities: getting the mapping and logging out this week so we can pinpoint any remaining p95 causes. :shipit: 
perf-bot: perf alert created: "amd-long-context-p95-regression" — monitoring enabled.
ashley: one more note — add a test that simulates KV cache cold + long-seq to avoid surprises.
marta: good call. adding to canary test plan.
